recommended_actions.headline: Remove or cite 1 unsourced statistical claim
recommended_actions.detail: Unsourced numeric claim detected on this page (one of these is repeated 2+ times on the page). Example: "30% of UK adults now actively pursuing photography as a hobby, there's never been a better time to develop your skills w". Either delete the claim or add a (Source: ONS / .gov / .ac.uk) citation inline. LLMs increasingly discount answers that cite uncited stats.

recommended_actions.headline: Replace 1 low-authority outbound citation
recommended_actions.detail: Outbound link to allbachelordegrees.com treated as a citation. Swap for a recognised source: Royal Photographic Society, .gov.uk, ONS, BBC, Nature, or a peer university. Weak citation domains hurt trust on both human and LLM reads.

recommended_actions.headline: Rewrite the opening section into a factual 60–90 word answer to "photography courses"
recommended_actions.detail: Current opener reads as rhetorical/marketing copy (signals: rhetorical_question_open, aspirational_words_7, aspirational_high). Replace with one paragraph that directly answers "photography courses" in 60–90 words (levels, format, price-from, location, who it suits). Place it under the H1. Serves AI Overview extraction AND human conversion in one block.

recommended_actions.headline: Rewrite 3 of the existing FAQs around the local commercial intent ("photography courses" - cost, beginner pathway, 1-2-1 vs group, in-person vs online)
recommended_actions.detail: Existing FAQs are not pulling their weight for "photography courses". Replace 3 of them with question/answer pairs that match real PAA queries AND are specific to this page's offering. Skip generic "what is photography" rewrites — they don't move conversion or AIO extraction.

recommended_actions.headline: Cite 1 authoritative source in the answer block (may help)
recommended_actions.detail: It is believed (heuristic, not proven) that AIO favours pages citing recognised sources. In the direct-answer block for "photography courses", link out once to Royal Photographic Society, a .gov.uk / .ac.uk source, or another recognised authority. Skip low-authority blogs/aggregators — they hurt trust on both human and LLM reads.
